statement: Consider the experiments just specified, with |a| + |b| bounded. Assume the conclusions of 3.11, 3.5, and 3.1 for their original marginal laws. Individual reflecting constraints are ordinary one-sided sign walls, not pairs 0 ≤ hx ≤ ε with ε allowed to tend to zero. Fix 0 < r < R < 2, 1 < p < 2, and a desired defect parameter ρ > 0. There are fixed testing parameters, a step length Tρ > 0, good edges Gn and good wall sites Sg n, and positive weights we, wx ≤ 1 with the following properties. For either tail in (4.1), or for their signed difference, let En(Q) = ∑︂ e∈Gn, e⊂Q we|∇eu0|2 + ∑︂ x∈Sg n∩Q wx|u0(x)|2 . (4.2) In the two-tail statement the energies are added. In a free comparison the energy is that of z and there is no wall sum. Then EEn(Qr) ≤ C, E ∑︂ C: C∩Qr̸=∅ DC ≤ C. (4.3) Here C and DC have the preceding step-cluster meaning. The constants in (4.3) may depend on ρ, p, r, R and the average bounds. Defective boxes satisfy the prescribed sparse-animal bound. For every fixed q < ∞ and A < ∞, the normalized spatial sums of w−q, cluster-size moments, and hole-diameter moments are bounded by deterministic constants outside an event of probability O(n−A). The relevant finite collection of moment orders can be chosen in advance. Let Un be the extension over holes supplied by 3.5, with a fixed choice of the testing parameters. It can be set to zero on the exceptional event. In scaled coordinates, E∥Un∥2 W1,p(n−1Qr) ≤ C, E ∫ n,Qr |Un − u0| −→ 0. (4.4) In a free comparison subtract a local cutoff-weighted average from both Un and z0. Its gradient and dissipation estimates are unchanged. All these centered estimates are uniform in the size of the ambient domain. The same bounds hold for a rough one-sided adapted experiment with only z|P ≥ a, for u− = (a − z)+, and with zero extension behind a controlled observed boundary. They hold uniformly after replacing z by z/K, K ≥ 1, with bounded rescaled thresholds. Threshold-uniform specialization. In the one-sided case, for each threshold a satisfying the required condition z|P ≥ a, the weights may be chosen independently of a. With the original marginal moment bounds fixed, EEn (︁ (a − z)+; Qr )︁ + E∥U(a) n ∥2 W1,p(n−1Qr) ≤ C0(1 + a2 ). (4.5) Thus, when a = K ≥ 1 and the observed values satisfy z|P ≥ K, the energy and squared Sobolev norm of (1 − z/K)+ are bounded by 2C0, uniformly in K. For an ordinary simply connected polygon domain with identical fixed boundary data, the exterior- preserving construction in Lemma 4.7 gives a bounded W1,p(R2) extension which is exactly zero outside the lattice polygon. This construction uses connectivity of its zero exterior; it is not asserted for an arbitrary disconnected internal observed set. 18 If QR has no observations or individual walls, and Xn is sampled from normalized ambient volume in Qr, then n∇(Xn,Xn+e)z0 for each fixed lattice step e, n(z0(Xn + i) − z0(Xn)) for each fixed lattice offset i, and n supt≤T0 |zt(Xn) − z0(Xn)| are tight. Thus this untruncated conclusion has a fixed positive macroscopic free buffer. It also holds up to controlled observations when a = b, because the two tails then control z − a. For general a < b, corresponding tightness statements hold only for the controlled tails up to observations. Here T0 is one fixed sufficiently short step. Sampling is not conditioned on an arbitrarily small random free set. Finally these statements allow a drift difference bounded by cn−2, with bounded support on the macroscopic scale, including a sufficiently small smooth exponential tilt of either marginal. Constants may depend on a fixed bound for c; the smallness needed for the change of marginal law is that in 3.1.
